definition_zh: 鼓掌；喝彩；称赞；赞许
definition_en: to show approval by clapping the hands, or to praise a person, action, or idea
core_image: 双手拍在一起的声音：用掌声把喜欢和赞成表达出来
scene: 演出结束，观众纷纷起身。The audience stood up to applaud the pianist after her final piece.
sceneCN: 这里 applaud 是「鼓掌；喝彩」（第 1 个义项：拍手表示赞赏）；句意为「钢琴家弹完最后一曲后，观众起身为她鼓掌」。这个词既可以指真实的拍手动作，也可以引申为口头或态度上的称赞。

pos.zh: 称赞；赞许（某人、某行为或某决定）

derivatives.zh: applaud 加名词后缀 -se 构成，义为「鼓掌；掌声；喝彩」
applaud 加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「鼓掌者；称赞者」
applaud 加形容词后缀 -able 的少见变体，义为「值得称赞的」，更常用 plausible 之外的形式 praiseworthy 表达

senses.title: To clap the hands to show enjoyment
senses.definition: to hit your hands together repeatedly to show that you enjoyed a performance
senses.definitionCN: 反复拍手，表示欣赏演出或表演
senses.example: The audience applauded loudly at the end of the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会结束时，观众热烈鼓掌。
senses.why: The core image is hands coming together to make sound; the most direct use is the physical clap itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是双手相击发出声响；最直接的用法就是拍手这个物理动作本身。

senses.title: To clap to welcome or thank someone
senses.definition: to clap in order to welcome a person onto a stage or to thank them
senses.definitionCN: 以掌声欢迎某人上台，或以掌声表示感谢
senses.example: Please applaud our next speaker as she comes to the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 下一位演讲者上台时，请大家鼓掌欢迎。
senses.why: The clap is directed at a person as a social gesture, extending the physical action to a ritual of welcome or thanks.
senses.whyCN: 掌声指向某个人，成为一种社交姿态；物理动作延伸为欢迎或致谢的仪式。

senses.title: To praise a performance or achievement publicly
senses.definition: to publicly praise a performance, work, or achievement, especially in the media
senses.definitionCN: 公开称赞演出、作品或成就，尤见于媒体报道
senses.example: Critics applauded the young director's first film.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家们盛赞这位年轻导演的首部电影。
senses.why: Approval that once needed clapping can now be expressed in words; the sound of praise replaces the sound of hands.
senses.whyCN: 原本需要鼓掌表达的赞许，如今可以用言语表达；赞许之声取代了拍手之声。

senses.title: To express strong approval of a decision or action
senses.definition: to say or show that you strongly approve of a decision, action, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 表示强烈赞成某个决定、行为或想法
senses.example: Environmental groups applauded the government's new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 环保团体对政府的新政策表示赞许。
senses.why: When the object is abstract, applaud no longer means clapping but standing behind something with approval.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是抽象事物时，applaud 不再指拍手，而是表示对某事的认同与支持。

senses.title: To praise someone for a specific quality or effort
senses.titleCN: 因品质或努力而称赞某人
senses.definition: to praise a person for a particular quality, effort, or courage, often with for
senses.definitionCN: 常与 for 连用，因某种品质、努力或勇气而称赞某人
senses.example: Teachers applauded the students for their honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们称赞学生诚实。
senses.why: The pattern applaud sb for sth treats praise as a reward given to a person, like applause given to a performer.
senses.whyCN: applaud sb for sth 结构把称赞看作给一个人的奖励，正如把掌声献给表演者。

senses.title: To be worthy of praise
senses.definition: to deserve praise, used in passive or descriptive sentences about actions or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动或描述性句子，指行为或品质值得称赞
senses.example: His courage in speaking up deserves to be applauded.
senses.exampleCN: 他敢于发声的勇气值得称道。
senses.why: Approval as a reward can be described as owed; something so good that it should receive the clap of praise.
senses.whyCN: 赞许作为一种奖励，可被描述为「应得的」；好到理应收获掌声的赞美。

intro.en: Applaud comes from Latin via Italian, built on a root meaning to clap or strike together.
intro.cn: applaud 经意大利语进入英语，词根义为「拍击；相击而响」。

items.en: Latin applaudere, from ad- (toward) + plaudere (to clap, strike), meaning to clap in approval.
items.cn: 拉丁语 applaudere，由 ad-（朝向）+ plaudere（拍击）构成，义为「拍手表示赞成」。

items.en: The compound verb spread in Late Latin and gave related forms like plausus, a clapping or a sound of approval.
items.cn: 这一复合动词在晚期拉丁语中通行，并派生出 plausus（拍打声；赞许声）等相关形式。

items.en: The word passed into Italian as applaudire before entering English.
items.cn: 该词先进入意大利语，作 applaudire，随后进入英语。

items.en: Applaud is first recorded in English in the late 1500s, at first meaning to clap or express approval.
items.cn: applaud 于十六世纪末在英语中首次见于记载，最初义为拍手或表示赞许。

items.en: The sense broadened from literal clapping to public and figurative praise of ideas, decisions, and people.
items.cn: 词义从字面鼓掌扩展为对想法、决定和人物的公开或比喻性称赞。

note.en: These words share spelling or meaning patterns with applaud, but differ in force or usage.
note.cn: 以下词语与 applaud 在拼写或词义上相关，但在语气或用法上有区别。

entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指鼓掌的声音；掌声

entries.definition: a round fruit; only looks similar at the start of the word
entries.definitionCN: 一种水果；仅词首拼写相近，与 applaud 词源无关

entries.definition: to make a formal request; shares the prefix ap- but has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 申请；应用；与前缀 ap- 相同但词根不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: seeming reasonable; from the same Latin root plaudere
entries.definitionCN: 看似有理的；与 applaud 同源于拉丁语 plaudere，原义与掌声相关

entries.definition: to hit the hands together; plainer and more physical than applaud
entries.definitionCN: 拍手；比 applaud 更口语、更侧重动作本身

entries.definition: to express strong approval in words; general-purpose praise
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；用言语表达赞许，泛用性最强

entries.definition: to shout in support or joy; louder and more emotional than clapping
entries.definitionCN: 欢呼；以喊叫表示支持或高兴，比鼓掌情绪更外放
嘉奖；正式或官方的称赞，语气庄重

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its Latin parts and sound family.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语部件和声音家族来搭建这个词。

normal.en: ap- + plaud: the prefix ap- (toward) plus the root plaud (clap) makes 'clap toward someone'.
normal.cn: ap-（朝向）+ plaud（拍击）＝「朝某人拍手」，即鼓掌赞许。

normal.en: applause is the noun twin: you applaud, and the result is applause.
normal.cn: applause 是名词孪生兄弟：你 applaud（鼓掌），产生的就是 applause（掌声）。

normal.en: plausible shares the root plaud: what gets applause sounds plausible.
normal.cn: plausible 与 applaud 同根：能赢得掌声的说法，听起来就显得可信。

normal.en: Sound link: 'a-PLOD' — picture the audience plodding hands together again and again.
normal.cn: 读音联想「厄-普洛德」：想象观众双手像踏步一样一下一下拍个不停。

normal.en: Opposite pair: applaud to approve, boo to reject — a theatre needs both.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：applaud 表示赞成，boo 表示喝倒彩——剧院里两者都有。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting like friends shaking hands: approval made audible.
abstract.cn: 想象双手相会如友人握手：赞许被变成了声音。

abstract.en: Applaud is approval you can hear; praise is approval you can read.
abstract.cn: applaud 是听得见的赞许，praise 是读得到的赞许。

abstract.en: Think of a switch that turns liking into sound: press it, and the room claps.
abstract.cn: 把它想成把「喜欢」转换成声音的开关：一按，满堂掌声。

examples.en: The whole audience applauded when the singer came on stage.
examples.cn: 歌手登台时，全场观众鼓掌。

examples.en: We applaud her decision to continue her studies.
examples.cn: 我们赞许她继续深造的决定。

examples.en: His speech was warmly applauded by the teachers.
examples.cn: 他的演讲赢得老师们热烈的掌声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆劳的」——阿婆看得劳累的演出结束时也劳着双手鼓掌，掌声不断，声似「阿婆劳的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 applaudere：前缀 ad-（朝向）+ 词根 plaudere（拍击；拍手作响）。词根 plaud- 还见于 applause（掌声）与 plausible（貌似有理的，原义「值得掌声的」）。拉丁词形确凿，无存疑。

sensesIntro.en: From the physical clap, the word grows into welcoming, praising, and approving.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从「拍手」这一物理动作出发，延伸为欢迎、称赞与认同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands striking together to turn approval into sound
core.cn: 核心意象：双手相击，把赞许变成听得见的声音

branches.en: The literal clap: enjoying a show or greeting a person with sound.
branches.cn: 字面拍手：为演出喝彩，或以掌声欢迎某人。

branches.en: Praise in words replaces clapping for works and performances.
branches.cn: 对作品与演出，言语称赞取代了拍手。

branches.en: Approval extends to decisions, policies, and ideas.
branches.cn: 赞许扩展到决定、政策与想法。

branches.en: Praise becomes personal: applauding someone for a quality.
branches.cn: 称赞变得具体：因某种品质而称赞某人。

branches.en: Approval turns into a reward that good actions deserve.
branches.cn: 赞许变成好行为应得的奖励。

intro.en: Applaud is built from a Latin prefix and a sound-related root, with a small word family.
intro.cn: applaud 由拉丁语前缀和与声音相关的词根构成，并有一个不大的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root plaud- also appears in other English and Latin words about striking and approval.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 plaud- 还出现在其他与拍击、赞许相关的英语及拉丁语词中。

items.example: In applaud, the clap is directed toward the performer.
items.exampleCN: 在 applaud 中，拍击朝向表演者。

items.example: Plaudere is the Latin verb behind applaud.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁动词 plaudere 是 applaud 的来源。

items.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词不定式词尾
items.example: Plaudere shows the raw dictionary form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: plaudere 展示该动词的原始词形。

items.meaningCN: 掌声；以声音表示的赞许
items.exampleCN: 雷鸣般的掌声响彻大厅。

items.meaning: seeming worthy of applause, hence believable
items.meaningCN: 貌似可信的；原义「值得掌声的」

items.example: The root also gave explosion, a sound of bursting.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还派生出 explosion（爆炸），指爆裂之声。

items.example: Every applauder added to the noise.
items.exampleCN: 每位鼓掌者都让声响更大。

items.meaning: the act of clapping in progress
items.example: The applauding crowd would not stop.
items.exampleCN: 鼓掌的人群久久不肯停下。

latinEntries.meaning: a clapping; a sound of approval

definition_zh: 苹果；苹果树
definition_en: a round fruit with firm white flesh and a green, red, or yellow skin
core_image: 果盘里一只红苹果，表皮还带着水珠
scene: 早餐桌上摆着面包、牛奶，还有一只洗干净的苹果。She sliced an apple for the child.
sceneCN: 这里 apple 是「苹果」（第 1 个义项：这种圆形果实）；句意是她给孩子切了一只苹果。

senses.title: The round fruit
senses.definition: a firm round fruit that grows on a tree and is eaten raw or cooked
senses.definitionCN: 长在树上、可生吃或烹煮的坚实圆形果实
senses.example: She sliced an apple for the child.
senses.exampleCN: 她给孩子切了一只苹果。
senses.why: Old English æppel meant simply 'apple' and could name any fruit; over time it narrowed to the one fruit we now mean.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 æppel 本义就是「苹果」，也能泛指果实；后来才收窄为今天这一种水果。

senses.title: The tree that bears it
senses.definition: used in compounds such as apple tree for the tree itself
senses.definitionCN: 用于 apple tree 等复合词，指苹果树本身
senses.example: An old apple stands at the garden's edge.
senses.exampleCN: 花园边上立着一棵老苹果树。
senses.why: English often uses the fruit name for the plant, as with cherry and plum, so apple can stand for the tree in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用果实名代指植物，樱桃与李子都是如此，所以在复合词里 apple 可以指树。

intro.en: Apple is an old Germanic word that once covered fruit in general.
intro.cn: apple 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，曾泛指各种果实。

items.en: The reconstructed root meant 'apple' and possibly any tree fruit.
items.cn: 重构词根意为「苹果」，也可能泛指树上的果实。

items.en: æppel was the ordinary word for apple and for fruit.
items.cn: æppel 是「苹果」及「果实」的常用词。

items.en: The form shifted toward the modern apple.
items.cn: 词形逐渐演变为现代形式。

items.en: Recipes show apple used specifically for the orchard fruit.
items.cn: 食谱文献显示 apple 已专指果园里的那种水果。

items.en: The word now also appears in many fixed phrases and compounds.
items.cn: 现代这个词还出现在许多固定短语与复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group is orchard fruit; the near-meaning group is other round fruits.
note.cn: 形近组是果园水果；近义组是其他圆形水果。

entries.definition: a tropical fruit named for its look
a sweet fruit with a narrow top
a soft fruit with fuzzy skin
a small smooth fruit with a stone

normalIntro.en: Apple is one short word with a very long history.
normalIntro.cn: apple 是一个很短的词，却有很长的历史。

normal.en: An apple a day keeps the doctor away is a well-known saying.
normal.cn: 「每天一苹果，医生远离我」是著名谚语。

normal.en: Apple pie is the classic compound.
normal.cn: apple pie 是最经典的复合词。

normal.en: The apple of one's eye means a much-loved person.
normal.cn: the apple of one's eye 意为掌上明珠。

normal.en: In compounds the fruit name can mean the tree: apple tree.
normal.cn: 复合词里果实名可指树：apple tree。

normal.en: The plural is apples, with a voiced s.
normal.cn: 复数是 apples，s 读浊音。

abstract.en: See a red apple with water still on the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象红苹果表皮还挂着水珠。

abstract.en: See a knife curling a strip of peel.
abstract.cn: 想象小刀削出一圈果皮。

abstract.en: See a branch bent low with fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象被果实压弯的树枝。

examples.cn: 她给孩子切了一只苹果。

examples.en: An old apple stands at the garden's edge.
examples.cn: 花园边上立着一棵老苹果树。

examples.en: He packed an apple and a sandwich for lunch.
examples.cn: 他装了一只苹果和一个三明治当午饭。

root: 古英语 æppel 源自原始日耳曼语，本可泛指果实，后专指苹果；同族词有 pineapple、apple pie 等复合形式。

sensesIntro.en: The fruit and, in compounds, the tree that bears it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一是指果实，二是在复合词中指结出果实的树。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round fruit held in the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心托着的一只圆果。

intro.en: A native Germanic word that forms many compounds.
intro.cn: 这是一个本族日耳曼语词，能构成许多复合词。

definition_zh: 申请人；求职者；报名者
definition_en: a person who formally asks for a job, a place, or a service
core_image: 手里捏着一叠材料站在窗口前的人
scene: 招聘会门口排着队，每个人都拿着简历。Each applicant was interviewed for ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 applicant 是「申请人；求职者」（第 1 个义项：正式提出申请的人）；句意是每位申请人都面谈了十分钟。

pos.zh: 名词：申请人；求职者；报名者

collocations.zh: 把申请人列入候选名单

senses.title: A person who applies for a job
senses.definition: someone who formally asks to be considered for a post or a place
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求被考虑录用或录取的人
senses.example: Each applicant was interviewed for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 每位申请人都面谈了十分钟。
senses.why: Applicant is the person noun from apply, with -ant marking the one who performs the action of applying.
senses.whyCN: applicant 是 apply 派生的指人名词，词尾 -ant 标示执行「申请」这一动作的人。

senses.title: A person making a formal request
senses.definition: someone who applies for a document, a benefit, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为某种证件、补助或服务提出申请的人
senses.example: The visa applicant must bring two photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 签证申请人必须带两张照片。
senses.why: The same -ant person noun serves every kind of formal request, not only employment.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ant 指人名词适用于各种正式请求，不只用于求职。

intro.en: Applicant is apply plus the Latin person ending -ant.
intro.cn: applicant 是 apply 加拉丁语指人词尾 -ant。

items.en: applicare meant 'to attach oneself to'.
items.cn: applicare 意为「使自己附着于」。

items.en: applicans was the present participle, 'one attaching himself'.
items.cn: applicans 是现在分词，意为「使自己靠近的人」。

items.en: English applicant first meant a person who applies for something.
items.cn: 英语 applicant 最初指为某事提出申请的人。

items.en: With modern employment it became the standard word for a job seeker.
items.cn: 随着现代就业制度，它成为求职者的标准说法。

items.en: The word now covers visas, grants, and school places as well.
items.cn: 现代它还涵盖签证、补助与入学名额。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other words for people who seek something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 apply 词根；近义组是其他表示寻求者身份的词。

entries.definition: a person competing for a post
a person put forward for a role

normalIntro.en: An applicant is the -ant person who does the applying.
normalIntro.cn: applicant 就是执行 apply 这个动作的 -ant 指人名词。

normal.en: Applicant for a post, applicant to a school.
normal.cn: 职位用 applicant for，学校用 applicant to。

normal.en: Job applicant is the most common pair.
normal.cn: job applicant 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The plural applicants is regular.
normal.cn: 复数 applicants 是规则变化。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AP-pli-cant.

abstract.en: See a desk with a name called out.

abstract.en: See a stamp landing on a form.

examples.en: Each applicant was interviewed for ten minutes.
examples.cn: 每位申请人都面谈了十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（申请）加 -ant（人）：提出申请的人。

root: 由 apply 加拉丁语指人词尾 -ant 构成，源自拉丁语 applicans「使自己靠近的人」；apply 的词根为 plicare「折叠」。

sensesIntro.en: One person noun covers job seekers and anyone else making a formal request.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个指人名词既指求职者，也指任何提出正式申请的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stepping forward with papers in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：拿着材料走上前的人。

intro.en: A Latin -ant person noun on the apply root.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在 apply 词根上的拉丁语 -ant 指人名词。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -ant marks the doer, as in applicant and claimant.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -ant 标示动作执行者，如 applicant 与 claimant。

definition_zh: 申请；申请书；应用；涂抹；专注
definition_en: a formal request, the act of putting something to use, a substance spread on a surface, or close attention

senses.title: A formal request
senses.definition: a written or spoken request for a job, a place, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额或服务提出的书面或口头请求
senses.example: Her application arrived before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她的申请在截止日期前寄到了。
senses.why: Application is the noun of apply, and the oldest formal sense is the act of asking, which then named the papers carrying the request.
senses.whyCN: application 是 apply 的名词，最早的正式义就是「提出请求」这一行为，之后又指承载请求的文件。

senses.title: The act of putting to use
senses.definition: the use of an idea, method, or substance in a practical situation
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、方法或物质用于实际情形
senses.example: The application of this theory is not simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论的应用并不简单。
senses.why: To apply is literally to lay something onto a surface, so application keeps the image of a method being laid onto a problem.
senses.whyCN: apply 字面就是把某物贴到一个表面上，所以 application 保留了「把方法贴到问题上」的意象。

senses.title: A substance spread on
senses.definition: a quantity of cream, paint, or medicine put onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面上的一定量的乳霜、颜料或药物
senses.example: A thin application of oil will protect the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 薄薄涂一层油可以保护木材。
senses.why: The physical sense of laying something on survives in this concrete use of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 把东西贴上去的物理含义，在这个具体的名词用法中保留下来。

senses.title: Close attention to a task
senses.definition: the quality of giving steady attention to work or study
senses.definitionCN: 对工作或学习持续投入注意力的品质
senses.example: Success here depends on steady application.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的成功取决于持续的专注。
senses.why: If the mind is applied to a task, it is bent onto it, and that effort became a sense of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果心思被「贴」在任务上，就是弯着身子扑在上面，这种用力成了名词的一个义项。

scene: 刷墙的师傅把滚筒按进漆里，再一点点推上去。Apply the paint in thin layers.

senses.title: To make a formal request
senses.definition: to ask officially for a job, a place, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求职位、名额或许可
senses.example: She applied for a place at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了这所学院的一个名额。
senses.why: Latin applicare meant 'to attach oneself to', and a candidate who applies attaches himself to an institution by request.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 意为「使自己附着于」，提出申请的候选人正是用请求把自己附着到某个机构上。

senses.title: To put something to use
senses.definition: to use a rule, method, or idea in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情形中使用规则、方法或观念
senses.example: He applied the same method to a harder problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他把同样的方法用到更难的题上。
senses.why: The original image is laying one thing onto another, so applying a method is laying it onto a case.
senses.whyCN: 本来的意象是把一样东西贴到另一样上，所以 apply 一个方法就是把它贴到一个情形上。

senses.title: To spread something on a surface
senses.definition: to put a substance such as paint or cream onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把颜料、乳霜等物质涂到表面上
senses.example: Apply the paint in thin layers.
senses.exampleCN: 把颜料薄薄地涂上几层。
senses.why: This is the most physical sense and the closest to the Latin verb's literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这是最物理的义项，也最接近拉丁语动词的字面含义。

senses.title: To be relevant to
senses.definition: to concern or be valid for a person or case
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某情形有关，或对其有效
senses.example: The ban applies to all vehicles.
senses.exampleCN: 这项禁令适用于所有车辆。
senses.why: If a rule can be laid onto a case, the rule reaches that case, which is the intransitive sense with to.
senses.whyCN: 如果一条规则能贴到一个情形上，这条规则就触及该情形，这就是与 to 连用的不及物用法。

senses.title: An arranged meeting

senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appretiare 意为「给……定价」，由 ad 与 pretium「价格」构成；appreciate 首先就是正确估量一件事物的价值。

senses.title: To be grateful for
senses.definition: to feel thankful for something someone has done
senses.definitionCN: 对别人所做的事心怀感谢
senses.example: I really appreciate your help with the report.
senses.exampleCN: 非常感谢你帮忙做这份报告。
senses.why: If you place a high value on a kindness, gratitude follows naturally, so the valuing sense produced the thanking sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果你把别人的好意估得很高，感激就自然产生，所以「估值」义衍生出「感谢」义。

senses.title: To understand fully
senses.definition: to be aware of how serious or important something is
senses.definitionCN: 意识到某事有多严重或多重要
senses.example: I appreciate that the decision was difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 我理解这个决定很难做。
senses.why: Valuing a situation properly requires seeing it clearly, which is why appreciate also means to grasp a fact.
senses.whyCN: 要恰当估量一个处境，必须先看清它，因此 appreciate 也有「领会事实」的意思。

senses.title: To rise in value
senses.definition: to increase in worth over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移价值上升
senses.example: The house has appreciated since they bought it.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子自他们买下以来已经增值。
senses.why: The price root shows through most plainly here: the thing's price has gone up.
senses.whyCN: 「价格」词根在这里最直白：这件东西的价格上去了。

intro.en: Appreciate goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to set a price on'.
intro.cn: appreciate 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「定价」的动词。

items.en: pretium meant 'price, value'.
items.cn: pretium 意为「价格、价值」。

items.en: appretiare meant 'to value or appraise'.
items.cn: appretiare 意为「估价」。

items.en: The past participle supplied the base of the English verb.
items.cn: 过去分词形式构成英语动词的基础。

items.en: English appreciate first meant 'to estimate the worth of'.
items.cn: 英语 appreciate 最初意为「估计价值」。

items.en: The senses of enjoying, thanking, and rising in price all developed from that estimate.
items.cn: 欣赏、感谢与增值三义都从这种估价发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the price root; the near-meaning group gives other words of valuing.
note.cn: 形近组共享「价格」词根；近义组是其他表示珍视的词。

normalIntro.en: To appreciate is to put the right price on something.
normalIntro.cn: appreciate 就是给一件事物标上恰当的价格。

normal.en: I appreciate your help is the standard polite thanks.
normal.cn: I appreciate your help 是标准的礼貌致谢。

normal.en: Appreciate that introduces an understood fact.
normal.cn: appreciate that 引出你已理解的事实。

normal.en: The noun is appreciation, as in a letter of appreciation.
normal.cn: 名词是 appreciation，如 a letter of appreciation。

normal.en: Property can appreciate, meaning rise in value.

abstract.en: See a hand pressed to the chest in thanks.

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 preci（价格）加 -ate：给足价钱，就是看重、欣赏。

sensesIntro.en: Setting a price leads to enjoying worth, thanking a kindness, grasping a fact, and rising in value.
sensesIntro.cn: 给事物定价，进而生出欣赏价值、感谢好意、理解事实与价值上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning an object over to judge its worth.
core.cn: 核心意象：把物件翻来覆去看它的价值。

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricing that now covers taste, thanks, and finance.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示定价的拉丁动词，如今涵盖品味、感谢与金融。

latinIntro.en: The root pretium, 'price', also gives precious and depreciate.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 pretium「价格」也派生出 precious 与 depreciate。

definition_zh: 估价；评估；赏识；感激；增值；货币升值；鉴赏
definition_en: the act of estimating the quality or worth of something; recognition of value; gratitude; an increase in value; also a written or spoken expression of approval
core_image: 把一件东西放上估价的天平：先称出它值多少，再承认它值钱，最后为这份价值心生感激
scene: 在画廊里，鉴定师在灯下端详一件小铜像，写下估值。Its appreciation took three experts two days.
sceneCN: 这里 appreciation 是「估价；评估价值」（第 1 个义项：判断某物的品质与价值）；句意：这件小铜像的估价花了三位专家两天时间。

pos.zh: 估价；评估；赏识；感激；增值；鉴赏

senses.title: Estimating worth: putting a value on something
senses.titleCN: 估定价值：给某物定个价
senses.definition: the act of estimating the quality, condition, or monetary worth of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的品质、状况或金钱价值的行为
senses.example: The appreciation of the painting took three experts two days.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴定这幅画的价值花了三位专家两天时间。
senses.why: Late Latin appretiare is ad- 'to' plus pretium 'price': to set a price on a thing. The first English sense, recorded c.1600, is exactly this act of estimating quality and worth.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 appretiare 是 ad-“向”加 pretium“价格”：给某物定个价。英语最早记录于约 1600 年的义项，正是这种判断品质与价值的行为。

senses.title: Recognition of value: esteeming what is good
senses.definition: a favorable estimate of someone or something; the recognition that something is valuable or excellent
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的高评价；承认某物有价值或很出色的认识
senses.example: Her appreciation of the old craftsman's skill grew with every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 每去一次，她对这位老匠人技艺的赏识就多一分。
senses.why: If the estimated worth is high, the estimate becomes esteem. After c.1650 appreciation commonly carried this 'high estimate' sense: the scale tips upward and the word names recognition rather than mere measurement.
senses.whyCN: 如果估出的价值很高，估价就变成器重。约 1650 年之后，appreciation 通常带有“高估”之义：天平向上倾斜，词义也从单纯的测量转为“认出价值”。

senses.title: Gratitude: valuing what someone has done
senses.titleCN: 感激：珍视别人所做之事
senses.definition: the feeling of being thankful for a kindness or benefit, and of recognizing its worth
senses.definitionCN: 因受到善意或帮助而心存感谢，并承认这份好处的价值
senses.example: He wrote a short note of appreciation to the nurse who stayed late.
senses.exampleCN: 他给那位守到很晚的护士写了一张简短的感谢便条。
senses.why: The thing now valued is another person's act. To appreciate a kindness is to put a high worth on it, and that estimate surfaces as gratitude — the emotional form of 'it was worth a lot to me'.
senses.whyCN: 此时被估价的是他人的行为。appreciate 一份善意，就是给它很高的价值，而这份估价浮上来就成感激——也就是“这对我很值”的情感形式。

senses.title: Rise in value: the asset gains worth
senses.definition: an increase in the value of property, shares, or other assets over time
senses.definitionCN: 房产、股票或其他资产随时间而增加的价值
senses.example: The house's appreciation paid for their daughter's tuition.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子的增值支付了他们女儿的学费。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the act of valuing to the value itself moving upward. The 1784 sense 'a rise in value' is the price side of pretium growing, not a new estimate being made.
senses.whyCN: 名词从“估价的动作”转到“价值本身向上走”。1784 年出现的“价值上升”义，是 pretium 的“价格”一面在增长，而不是又做了一次估价。

senses.title: A formal valuation: the official figure
senses.titleCN: 正式估价：官方核定的数字
senses.definition: a formal assessment of value, as for tax, insurance, or sale, often recorded as a figure
senses.definitionCN: 为税务、保险或出售而做的正式价值评估，通常落成一个数字
senses.example: The insurance appreciation came in well below the rebuild cost.
senses.exampleCN: 保险估价远低于重建成本。
senses.why: The 1799 sense 'act of setting a value on' narrows the first sense into an official act. Here the estimate is written down and binding, so appreciation becomes a valuation document rather than a private judgment.
senses.whyCN: 1799 年出现的“给某物定价的行为”把最早义项收窄为一种官方行为。此时估价被写下来并具有约束力，appreciation 也就从私人判断变成一份估价文件。

senses.title: An expression of approval: the words of praise
senses.titleCN: 赞赏之辞：说出来的好评
senses.definition: a spoken or written statement that recognizes the good qualities of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面承认某人某物优点的表述
senses.example: The review was a warm appreciation of the young pianist.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇评论是对这位年轻钢琴家的热情赞赏。
senses.why: The 1858 sense 'expression of favorable estimation' externalizes the inner estimate. What was a judgment in the mind becomes words; the noun now names the tribute rather than the appraisal.
senses.whyCN: 1858 年出现的“表达有利评价”把内心的估价外化。原本在心里的判断变成了话语；名词此时命名的是称许，而不是评估过程。

senses.title: Understanding the significance: seeing why it matters
senses.titleCN: 体认意义：明白它为何重要
senses.definition: a clear understanding of the importance, difficulty, or meaning of something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的重要性、难度或意义的清楚理解
senses.example: Living through the drought gave them a new appreciation of water.
senses.exampleCN: 经历过那场干旱，他们对水有了新的体会。
senses.why: To value something fully you must see what it costs or what it does. This branch moves from worth to understanding: the estimate is now a grasp of significance, as in an appreciation of the difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 要真正看重某物，必须看见它的代价或作用。这条分支从“价值”转到“理解”：估价在这里变成对意义的把握，如 appreciation of the difficulty（对困难的认识）。

senses.title: Currency appreciation: the money grows stronger
senses.titleCN: 货币升值：钱变得更值钱
senses.definition: an increase in the exchange value of a currency relative to other currencies
senses.definitionCN: 一种货币相对于其他货币的汇兑价值上升
senses.example: A sharp appreciation of the yen made imports cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 日元的急剧升值让进口商品变便宜了。
senses.why: This is the asset sense applied to a whole currency: its price in other currencies rises. The word still measures worth, but the worth being measured is the money itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是资产义应用到整种货币上：它以其他货币计的价格上升。这个词仍在衡量价值，只是被衡量的对象变成了钱本身。

senses.title: Aesthetic appreciation: taste trained on art
senses.titleCN: 审美鉴赏：被艺术训练过的眼光
senses.definition: the trained enjoyment and evaluation of art, music, or beauty, based on discernment rather than mere liking
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术、音乐或美的有训练的欣赏与评价，基于鉴别力而非单纯喜欢
senses.example: The course teaches the appreciation of Renaissance painting.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课教授文艺复兴绘画的鉴赏。
senses.why: The recognition sense is applied to beauty: the viewer estimates quality, feels its worth, and is pleased. Aesthetic appreciation is thus valuation and gratitude-like delight fused into taste.
senses.whyCN: “认出价值”的义项被用到美上：观者判断品质，感到它可贵，并因此愉悦。审美鉴赏于是是估价与类似感激的喜悦融合成趣味。

intro.en: Appreciation entered English c.1600 from French appréciation, the action noun of apprécier, and behind both stands Late Latin appretiare 'estimate the quality of' — ad- 'to' plus pretium 'price'. The suffix -ion turns the act into a noun. Its family is the price family, not the proper family of appropriate and not the near family of approximate.
intro.cn: appreciation 约于 1600 年从法语 appréciation 进入英语，它是 apprécier 的动作名词；两者背后是晚期拉丁语 appretiare“评估品质”——ad-“向”加 pretium“价格”。后缀 -ion 把这个动作变成名词。它属于“价格”词族，既不是 appropriate 的“自己的”词族，也不是 approximate 的“最近”词族。

items.en: First recorded as 'act of estimating the quality and worth of something'. The earliest sense is valuation, not gratitude.
items.cn: 最早记录为“判断某物品质与价值的行为”。最早的义项是估价，而不是感激。

items.en: From French appréciation, the action noun of apprécier (14c.). French passed on both the noun and the verb pattern, with -tion marking an action or its result.
items.cn: 来自法语 appréciation，即 apprécier（14 世纪）的动作名词。法语把名词和动词模式一并传下，-tion 标记动作或其结果。

items.en: Appretiare 'estimate the quality of' = ad- 'to' + pretium 'price'. The verb literally sets a price on a thing, so worth and price are one idea at the root.
items.cn: appretiare“评估品质”= ad-“向”+ pretium“价格”。这个动词字面上就是给某物定价，因此在词根处，价值与价格是同一个概念。

items.en: After c.1650 the noun generally includes a 'high estimate'; 1784 adds 'a rise in value', and 1799 'act of setting a value on'. Esteem, market gain and official valuation split off from the first sense.
items.cn: 约 1650 年之后，这个词通常含有“高估”；1784 年增加“价值上升”义，1799 年增加“给某物定值的行为”义。器重、市场增值与官方估价从最早义项中分了出来。

items.en: Appreciate is recorded only in the 1650s, later than appreciation. The 1858 sense 'expression of favorable estimation' adds spoken or written praise.
items.cn: appreciate 直到 17 世纪 50 年代才有记录，晚于 appreciation。1858 年出现的“表达有利评价”义，增加了口头或书面的称许。

items.en: All senses still run through pretium 'price': estimate a price, value it highly, feel its worth, watch it rise. Appropriate (proprius 'one's own') and approximate (proximus 'nearest') are different roots that only look alike.
items.cn: 所有义项仍贯穿 pretium“价格”：估一个价、把价估高、感到它可贵、看着它上涨。appropriate（proprius“自己的”）与 approximate（proximus“最近的”）只是形近，词根完全不同。

note.en: The first group separates appreciation from two famous look-alikes that belong to different roots; the second group separates it from words of gratitude and valuation that share only part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把 appreciation 与两个著名的形近词分开，它们属于不同词根；第二组把它与只共享部分含义的“感激”和“估价”词分开。

entries.definition: to value, understand, be grateful for, or rise in value. It shares the pretium root, but it is recorded in the 1650s, later than appreciation c.1600.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；理解；感激；增值。它与 appreciation 共享 pretium 词根，但直到 17 世纪 50 年代才有记录，晚于约 1600 年的 appreciation。

entries.definition: suitable or proper for a purpose. It comes from proprius 'one's own', not from pretium 'price', so it is not a relative of appreciation.
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；恰当的。它来自 proprius“自己的”，而不是 pretium“价格”，因此不是 appreciation 的同族词。

entries.definition: close to the correct value but not exact. It comes from proximus 'nearest', a third root that merely looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 接近正确值但不精确的。它来自 proximus“最近的”，是第三个只是看起来相似的词根。

entries.definition: the feeling of being thankful. It covers only the emotional branch, while appreciation also means valuation and increase in value.
entries.definitionCN: 感激之情。它只覆盖情感分支，而 appreciation 还表示估价与增值。

entries.definition: the act of publicly acknowledging someone's merit or existence. It stresses acknowledgment, while appreciation stresses the high value placed on the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 公开承认某人的功绩或存在。它强调“承认”，而 appreciation 强调给某物很高的评价。

entries.definition: an expert or official estimate of monetary value. It is the technical valuation branch, while appreciation can also mean esteem or gratitude.
entries.definitionCN: 专家或官方对金钱价值的估算。它是技术性的估价分支，而 appreciation 还可以指器重或感激。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: pretium 'price', the documented dates c.1600 / 1650s / 1784 / 1799 / 1858, and the fixed phrases express appreciation and capital appreciation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：pretium“价格”，有据可查的年代 1600／17 世纪 50 年代／1784／1799／1858，以及 express appreciation、capital appreciation 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Pretium is 'price'. Appreciation begins as putting a price on a thing, which is why the word can mean valuation before it means gratitude.
normal.cn: pretium 是“价格”。appreciation 的起点是给某物定价，所以它会先表示估价，之后才表示感激。

normal.en: Appreciation is recorded c.1600 but appreciate only in the 1650s: the noun came first, and the verb followed.
normal.cn: appreciation 约记录于 1600 年，而 appreciate 到 17 世纪 50 年代才出现：名词先来，动词后到。

normal.en: Capital appreciation is the rise of an asset's price; currency appreciation is the rise of a currency against others.
normal.cn: capital appreciation 是资产价格上涨；currency appreciation 是一种货币对其他货币的升值。

normal.en: Express appreciation is the standard phrase for saying thank you in a formal setting.
normal.cn: express appreciation 是在正式场合表达感谢的标准说法。

normal.en: An appreciation of art is trained taste: the same word that prices a bronze bird also judges a painting.
normal.cn: an appreciation of art 是受过训练的趣味：给铜鸟估价的同一个词，也用来品评一幅画。

abstract.en: A balance with a small object on one pan and weights on the other: the needle settles, and the object now has a worth.
abstract.cn: 一架天平，一盘放小物件，一盘放砝码：指针停住，这件东西便有了价值。

abstract.en: The needle can move up two ways: someone raises the estimate, or the object itself becomes more valuable. Appreciation covers both.
abstract.cn: 指针可以向上走两种方式：有人提高估价，或物件本身变得更值钱。appreciation 两者都覆盖。

abstract.en: Once worth is felt as a personal gift, the scale turns into a thank-you note: valuation and gratitude are the same estimate seen from inside.
abstract.cn: 当价值被感受为一份私人馈赠，天平就变成一张感谢便条：估价与感激是同一个判断的内外两面。

examples.en: The audience showed its appreciation with a long round of applause.
examples.cn: 观众以长久的掌声表达赞赏。

examples.en: Land in the district has seen steady appreciation over ten years.
examples.cn: 这个区的土地十年来稳步增值。

examples.en: Travel gave her a deeper appreciation of how differently people live.
examples.cn: 旅行让她更深刻地体会到人们的生活方式有多么不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普瑞希爱申」——阿普（Ap）把画举到灯下估价，瑞希（Rui Xi）看得连连点头，爱申（Ai Shen）写下“很值钱” → appreciation 欣赏、感激、增值

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 appretiare“estimate the quality of”（ad-“向”+ pretium“价格”），核心是给事物定价、估出价值，再由“估得高”引申为赏识、感激与增值。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of appreciation all start from a pair of scales: something is priced, the price is judged high, the high worth is felt as gratitude, and the value itself may rise. Art, formal documents and currencies are later fields for the same estimate.
sensesIntro.cn: appreciation 的九个义项都从一架天平开始：给某物定价，判断价格很高，把这份高价值感受为感激，而价值本身还可能上涨。艺术、正式文件与货币只是这同一估价行为后来进入的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed on a scale and given a worth.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一件东西放上天平，给它一个价值。

branches.en: ESTIMATE AND VALUATION: the original act of judging worth, and its official, written form.
branches.cn: 估价与核价：判断价值的最初行为，以及它官方化、书面化的形式。

branches.en: RECOGNITION AND TASTE: esteeming what is excellent, including the trained appreciation of art.
branches.cn: 赏识与趣味：器重出色之物，包括受过训练的艺术鉴赏。

branches.en: GRATITUDE: the high estimate of a kindness, felt as thankfulness.
branches.cn: 感激：把一份善意估得很高，并在心里感受为感谢。

branches.en: ASSETS AND CURRENCY: worth that rises, whether in property or in money itself.
branches.cn: 资产与货币：价值向上走，无论对象是房产还是货币本身。

branches.en: PRAISE AND UNDERSTANDING: the estimate spoken aloud, and the grasp of why something matters.
branches.cn: 称许与理解：说出口的评价，以及对某物为何重要的把握。

intro.en: Appreciation is appreciat- plus -ion, from Latin -ionem, which names an action or its result. English builds appreciate, appreciative, appreciatively, appreciable, appreciably and unappreciated on the same stem, and de- gives the opposite depreciate.
intro.cn: appreciation 是 appreciat- 加 -ion，后者来自拉丁语 -ionem，命名动作或其结果。英语在同一词干上构造出 appreciate、appreciative、appreciatively、appreciable、appreciably 与 unappreciated，而 de- 给出反方向的 depreciate。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Late Latin appretiare, ad- plus pretium 'price'. Latin pretium also gives pretiare 'to price' and depretiare 'to lower the value of'; none of these belongs to proprius or proximus.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是晚期拉丁语 appretiare，即 ad- 加 pretium“价格”。拉丁语 pretium 还给出 pretiare“定价”与 depretiare“降低价值”；这些都不属于 proprius 或 proximus。

items.structure: appreciat- (set a value) + -ion (action or result noun)
items.meaning: valuation, esteem, gratitude, or increase in value
items.meaningCN: 估价；赏识；感激；增值（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: She showed her appreciation with a handwritten card.
items.exampleCN: 她用一张手写卡片表达感谢。

items.meaning: to value, understand, thank, or increase in worth
items.meaningCN: 重视；理解；感激；增值（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: I appreciate your help more than I can say.
items.exampleCN: 我对你的帮助感激不尽。

items.meaning: showing gratitude or sensitive to value
items.meaningCN: 感激的；有鉴赏力的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The audience was appreciative of the small ensemble.
items.exampleCN: 观众对这个小乐团很是欣赏。

items.meaning: in a grateful or admiring way
items.meaningCN: 感激地；赞赏地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She smiled appreciatively at the gift.
items.exampleCN: 她对这份礼物感激地笑了。

items.meaning: large enough to be noticed or measured
items.meaningCN: 可察觉的；相当可观的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: There was an appreciable drop in temperature.

items.meaningCN: 明显地；可观地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: not recognized or thanked for one's value
items.meaningCN: 未受赏识的；未被感激的（un- 表示否定）
items.exampleCN: 夜班员工觉得自己未受重视。

items.meaning: to fall in value, or to belittle
items.meaningCN: 贬值；贬低（de-“向下”+ preci-“价格”+ -ate）
items.example: The car depreciates as soon as it is driven away.

definition_zh: 接近；靠近；着手处理；方法；路径
definition_en: to come near in space or time, to begin dealing with something, or a way of doing it
core_image: 沿着小路一步步走近山脚
scene: 天色暗下来，远处那盏灯越来越清楚。The train slowed as it approached the station.
sceneCN: 这里 approach 是「接近」（第 1 个义项：在空间上靠近）；句意是火车进站时慢了下来。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：平易近人的；可接近的

senses.title: To come near
senses.definition: to move closer to a place, a person, or a point in time
senses.definitionCN: 向某个地点、某个人或某个时间点靠近
senses.example: The train slowed as it approached the station.
senses.exampleCN: 火车进站时慢了下来。
senses.why: Latin appropiare came from ad, 'to', and prope, 'near', so approach is literally 'to come near'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appropiare 由 ad「向」与 prope「近」构成，所以 approach 字面就是「变近」。

senses.title: To begin dealing with
senses.definition: to start to handle a problem, a task, or a person in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式开始处理问题、任务或人
senses.example: We need to approach the issue calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要冷静地处理这个问题。
senses.why: Moving toward a problem is the first step in dealing with it, so the spatial verb became a verb of method.
senses.whyCN: 朝问题走过去就是处理它的第一步，于是这个空间动词变成了表示方法的动词。

senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.definition: a method or line of attack used to deal with something
senses.definitionCN: 处理某事所采用的方法或路线
senses.example: Her approach to teaching is very practical.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教学方法非常务实。
senses.why: The route by which you come at a task is the method you use, which is how the noun came to mean 'way'.
senses.whyCN: 你走向一项任务所取的路线就是所用方法，名词因此有了「方式」的意思。

intro.en: Approach comes from Latin words for 'to' and 'near'.
intro.cn: approach 来自拉丁语中表示「向」与「近」的词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向」。

items.en: prope meant 'near'.
items.cn: prope 意为「近」。

items.en: appropiare meant 'to come near'.
items.cn: appropiare 意为「靠近」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: The noun sense of a method developed from the idea of a way of coming at something.
items.cn: 名词的「方法」义从「走向某物的路径」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the near root; the near-meaning group gives other words for nearing and for methods.
note.cn: 形近组共享「近」词根；近义组是其他表示接近与方法的词。

entries.definition: to blame; only the spelling is close
entries.definitionCN: 责备；只是拼写相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Approach is moving prope, near, step by step.
normalIntro.cn: approach 就是一步步走近，拉丁语 prope 就是「近」。

normal.en: An approach to a problem uses to, not for.
normal.cn: 「处理问题的方法」用 approach to，不用 for。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling.
normal.cn: 名词与动词拼写相同。

normal.en: The approach of winter means its arrival.
normal.cn: the approach of winter 意为冬天临近。

normal.en: Approachable describes a person easy to talk to.
normal.cn: approachable 形容人平易近人。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PPROACH.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPROACH。

abstract.en: See a path narrowing toward a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象小路渐渐收向山脚。

abstract.en: See a train slowing into a lit platform.
abstract.cn: 想象火车减速驶入亮灯的站台。

abstract.en: See a hand reaching for a doorknob.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向门把。

examples.en: The train slowed as it approached the station.
examples.cn: 火车进站时慢了下来。

examples.en: We need to approach the issue calmly.
examples.cn: 我们需要冷静地处理这个问题。

examples.en: Her approach to teaching is very practical.
examples.cn: 她的教学方法非常务实。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 proach（近）：朝近处走，接近。

root: 来自拉丁语 appropiare「靠近」，由 ad「向」与 prope「近」构成，经古法语进入英语；由空间靠近引申出处理与方法。

sensesIntro.en: Coming near in space becomes coming to grips with a task, then the route taken to do it.
sensesIntro.cn: 空间上的靠近，变成对任务的着手，再变成所走的路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path that narrows toward its destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：渐渐收向目的地的小路。

intro.en: A Latin verb of nearing that English uses as noun and verb.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示靠近的拉丁动词，英语中兼作名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: The root prope, 'near', also gives proximity and approximate.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 prope「近」也派生出 proximity 与 approximate。

definition_zh: 合适的；恰当的；占用；拨用
definition_en: suitable for a particular situation, or to take something for one's own use
core_image: 在正式场合换上的一双皮鞋
scene: 葬礼上他换下了运动鞋，穿了一双深色皮鞋。Dark clothes are appropriate for the occasion.
sceneCN: 这里 appropriate 是「合适的」（第 1 个义项：与场合相称）；句意是深色衣服适合这个场合。

senses.title: Suitable for the situation
senses.definition: right or suitable for a particular purpose or occasion
senses.definitionCN: 对特定目的或场合而言是对的、相称的
senses.example: Dark clothes are appropriate for the occasion.
senses.exampleCN: 深色衣服适合这个场合。
senses.why: Latin appropriare meant 'to make one's own', from ad and proprius, 'own'; what is appropriate is what properly belongs to the case.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appropriare 意为「使成为自己的」，由 ad 与 proprius「自己的」构成；appropriate 就是本属于这个场合的东西。

senses.title: To take for one's own use
senses.definition: to take something, often without permission, and use it as your own
senses.definitionCN: 把某物（常未经许可）拿来当作自己的使用
senses.example: The company appropriated the land without warning.
senses.exampleCN: 公司未经通知就占用了这块地。
senses.why: The verb keeps the literal Latin sense of making a thing one's own, which can shade into seizing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「使成为自己的」字面义，这一层含义可以滑向「夺取」。

senses.title: To set aside money for a purpose
senses.definition: to formally assign funds or resources to a particular use
senses.definitionCN: 正式把资金或资源划归特定用途
senses.example: The council appropriated funds for the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 议会为新图书馆拨了款。
senses.why: Assigning money to a use is a legal way of making it belong to that purpose, so the same verb serves budgets.
senses.whyCN: 把钱划归某项用途，就是用法律方式让它属于那个目的，所以同一个动词也用于预算。

intro.en: Appropriate comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to make one's own'.
intro.cn: appropriate 来自拉丁语中意为「使成为自己的」的动词。

items.en: proprius meant 'one's own, particular'.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、专属的」。

items.en: appropriare meant 'to make one's own'.
items.cn: appropriare 意为「使成为自己的」。

items.en: The participle gave the adjective its form.
items.cn: 分词形式构成形容词的形态。

items.en: English appropriate first meant 'belonging to a person'.
items.cn: 英语 appropriate 最初意为「属于某人的」。

items.en: The sense widened to 'fitting the case' and the verb kept the sense of taking over.
items.cn: 词义扩展为「切合情形」，动词则保留「占为己有」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the own root; the near-meaning group gives other words for fitting.
note.cn: 形近组共享「自己的」词根；近义组是其他表示合适的词。

entries.definition: the act of taking or assigning

normalIntro.en: Appropriate means belonging to this case, this occasion, this purpose.
normalIntro.cn: appropriate 意为属于这个情形、这个场合、这个目的。

normal.en: Appropriate for an occasion, appropriate to a purpose.
normal.cn: 场合用 appropriate for，目的用 appropriate to。

normal.en: As appropriate means choose what fits each case.
normal.cn: as appropriate 意为酌情处理。

normal.en: The verb means take over or assign money.
normal.cn: 动词义为占用或拨款。

normal.en: Misappropriate is the crime of taking wrongly.
normal.cn: misappropriate 指挪用、侵吞。

normal.en: As an adjective stress the second syllable: a-PPRO-pri-ate.
normal.cn: 作形容词时重音在第二个音节：a-PPRO-pri-ate。

abstract.en: See polished shoes set beside gym shoes.
abstract.cn: 想象皮鞋摆在运动鞋旁。

abstract.en: See a key that belongs to one door only.
abstract.cn: 想象只属于一扇门的钥匙。

abstract.en: See a budget line marked for one project.
abstract.cn: 想象预算表上标注某一项目的那一行。

examples.en: Dark clothes are appropriate for the occasion.
examples.cn: 深色衣服适合这个场合。

examples.cn: 公司未经通知就占用了这块地。

examples.en: The council appropriated funds for the new library.
