dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 propri（自己的）加 -ate：属于这个场合的，合适的。

root: 来自拉丁语 appropriare「使成为自己的」，由 ad 与 proprius「自己的」构成；由「专属」发展出「合适」与「占用、拨款」。

sensesIntro.en: Belonging to the case gives fitness, and belonging to oneself gives taking and assigning.
sensesIntro.cn: 属于情形则「合适」，属于自己则「占用」与「拨用」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an item that belongs exactly to this occasion.
core.cn: 核心意象：恰好属于这个场合的一件东西。

intro.en: A Latin word of ownership that works as adjective and verb.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示归属的拉丁词，兼作形容词与动词。

latinIntro.en: The root proprius, 'one's own', also gives property and proper.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 proprius「自己的」也派生出 property 与 proper。

definition_zh: 赞成；同意；批准；核准
definition_en: to think that something is good or right, or to give official permission for it
core_image: 在文件末尾签下名字，表示同意
scene: 会议开到一半，主管在预算表上签了字。The committee approved the new budget by a show of hands.
sceneCN: 这里 approve 是「批准」（第 2 个义项：正式核准某事）；句意是委员会举手表决通过了新预算。

derivatives.zh: 动词：不赞成，与 approve 相对

senses.title: To think something is good
senses.definition: to consider something right or satisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事正确或令人满意
senses.example: My parents do not approve of late nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我父母不赞成熬夜。
senses.why: Latin probare meant 'to test and prove good', so to approve is to find a thing that has stood the test.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为「检验后证明是好的」，所以 approve 就是认定某物经得住检验。

senses.title: To give official permission
senses.definition: to accept a plan or request by formal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由有权的机构正式接受计划或请求
senses.example: The council approved the building plan last night.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会昨晚批准了这份建筑方案。
senses.why: The same testing sense entered official procedure: after examining a proposal, a body gives its consent.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「检验」义进入了官方程序：机构审查提案之后给出同意，就是批准。

intro.en: Approve goes back to a Latin verb for testing whether a thing is good.
intro.cn: approve 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「检验某物是否合格」的动词。

items.en: probus meant 'upright, honest, good'.
items.cn: probus 意为「正直、诚实、良好」。

items.en: probare meant 'to test, to prove'.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、证明」。

items.en: ad plus probare gave 'to assent to after testing'.
items.cn: ad 与 probare 结合，得到「检验后表示同意」。

items.en: The word passed into French as aprover, 'to consent to'.
items.cn: 这个词进入法语作 aprover，意为「同意」。

items.en: English approve first meant 'to prove', then narrowed to 'to judge good'.
items.cn: 英语 approve 最初意为「证明」，后来缩小为「判定为好」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the probare root; the near-meaning group lists other words of consent.
note.cn: 形近组共享 probare 词根；近义组是其他表示同意认可的词。

normalIntro.en: To approve is to sign off after checking.
normalIntro.cn: approve 就是检查之后签字放行。

normal.en: Approve of is the common pattern for opinions.
normal.cn: approve of 是表达看法时的常见搭配。

normal.en: Approve a plan takes a direct object.
normal.cn: 批准某方案时 approve 直接带宾语。

normal.en: The noun is approval, as in a nod of approval.
normal.cn: 名词是 approval，如点头表示赞许。

normal.en: The opposite verb is disapprove.
normal.cn: 反义动词是 disapprove。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: ap-PROVE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：ap-PROVE。

abstract.en: See a pen resting on a signed page.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔停在签好字的纸页上。

abstract.en: See a row of hands raised in a meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象会议上一排举起的手。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto a form.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压在表格上。

examples.en: My parents do not approve of late nights.
examples.cn: 我父母不赞成熬夜。

examples.en: The council approved the building plan last night.
examples.cn: 市议会昨晚批准了这份建筑方案。

examples.en: Her manager approves every expense over a hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 超过一百英镑的开支都要由她经理批准。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 prove（证明）：经过检验觉得好，于是点头同意。

root: 来自拉丁语 approbare「认可、证实」，由 ad「向」与 probare「检验、证明」构成；先检验再认可，故有赞成一义，又引申为官方批准。

sensesIntro.en: A thing is tested, judged good, and then either praised or formally allowed.
sensesIntro.cn: 事物先被检验，判为良好，随后或是被赞许，或是被正式放行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand signing at the foot of a document.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在文件末尾签下名字。

intro.en: A Latin verb of proving and consenting that still keeps both halves of its meaning.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示检验与同意的拉丁动词，两层含义至今都保留着。

latinIntro.en: The root probare, 'to test', also gives probable, prove and probation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 probare「检验」也派生出 probable、prove 与 probation。

definition_zh: 大约；大概；近似地
definition_en: used before a number to show that it is not exact, or to describe something as nearly but not exactly so
core_image: 秤杆停在差一点水平的位置
scene: 她在站台上看了好几次表。The journey takes approximately two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 approximately 是「大约」（第 1 个义项：用于数量或时间的不精确估计）；句意是这段路程大约要两个小时。

senses.title: About, before a number
senses.definition: used to give a figure that is close to the true one
senses.definitionCN: 给出一个接近真实值的数字
senses.example: The repair will take approximately three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理大约要三天。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective approximate into a marker placed before figures that are nearest rather than exact.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 approximate 变成标记词，专门放在那些「最接近而非精确」的数字前面。

senses.title: In a broadly similar way
senses.definition: used when two things are nearly, but not exactly, the same
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明两件事大体相同但并不完全一致
senses.example: The two methods are approximately equivalent in cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种方法在成本上大致相当。
senses.why: From counting, the word extends to comparing qualities: two things may stand near each other without matching exactly.
senses.whyCN: 从计数扩展到性质比较：两样东西可以彼此靠得很近，却并不完全吻合。

intro.en: Approximately is simply the adjective approximate with the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: approximately 就是形容词 approximate 加上副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: prope meant 'near'.
items.cn: prope 意为「近」。

items.en: The superlative proximus meant 'nearest'.
items.cn: 最高级 proximus 意为「最近的」。

items.en: approximare meant 'to come near'.
items.cn: approximare 意为「靠近」。

items.en: English formed the adjective approximate from the Latin verb.
items.cn: 英语由这个拉丁动词造出形容词 approximate。

items.en: Adding -ly produced the everyday adverb for rough figures.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 之后，形成了日常用来修饰约数的副词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the root; the near-meaning group gives other hedges for numbers.
note.cn: 形近组同根；近义组是其他用来给数字留余地的词。

normalIntro.en: Approximately softens a number so it is not a promise.
normalIntro.cn: approximately 让数字变得柔和，不再像承诺。

normal.en: It usually sits right before the figure.
normal.cn: 它通常紧挨在数字前面。

normal.en: In speech people often shorten it to about.
normal.cn: 口语里人们常把它换成 about。

normal.en: The adjective form drops the -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词形式去掉 -ly。

normal.en: It can also compare two things as broadly equal.
normal.cn: 它也能表示两件事大体相等。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: ap-PROX-i-mate-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：ap-PROX-i-mate-ly。

abstract.en: See a needle stopping a hair below the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象指针停在刻度下方一点点。

abstract.en: See two lines that almost, not quite, meet.
abstract.cn: 想象两条几乎相接却未相接的线。

abstract.en: See a hand waving to mean roughly so.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手左右摆动表示大概如此。

examples.en: The journey takes approximately two hours.
examples.cn: 这段路程大约要两个小时。

examples.en: The repair will take approximately three days.
examples.cn: 这次修理大约要三天。

examples.en: The two methods are approximately equivalent in cost.
examples.cn: 这两种方法在成本上大致相当。

dict_mnemonic.text: approximate（近似的）加 -ly：以近似的方式，就是大约。

root: 由形容词 approximate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；approximate 源自拉丁语 approximare「靠近」，其词根 proximus 意为「最近的」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb covers both a rough figure and a rough match between things.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词既修饰粗略的数字，也描述事物之间大致的吻合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weighing scale resting a little off level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平略微偏离水平。

intro.en: An adverb made by adding -ly to a Latin-derived adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个由拉丁来源形容词加 -ly 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The root prope, 'near', also lies behind proximity.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 prope「近」也是 proximity 的来源。

definition_zh: 围裙；停机坪；（舞台前缘的）台口
definition_en: a piece of clothing worn over the front of other clothes to keep them clean; also the area where aircraft park at an airport
core_image: 挡在前面的布：一块布挡在身前护住里面的衣服
scene: 妈妈系好围裙开始做饭。The chef put on an apron before starting to cook in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 apron 是「围裙」（第 1 个义项：护住身前的衣物）；句意为「厨师在下厨前系上了围裙」。该词还可指机场的停机坪或舞台前缘。

pos.zh: 停机坪（机场内飞机停放、装卸的区域）

collocations.phrase: wipe one's hands on the apron

derivatives.zh: apron 加形容词性后缀 -ed 构成，义为「系着围裙的」，多作定语描写人物形象
apron 加否定前缀 un- 与后缀 -ed 构成的少见形容词，义为「未系围裙的」，仅用于描写性语境

senses.title: A garment worn to protect clothes
senses.definition: a piece of cloth tied over the front of the body to keep the clothes underneath clean while cooking or working
senses.definitionCN: 系在身前的布片，做饭或干活时保护里面的衣服不被弄脏
senses.example: Grandma wears a floral apron when she makes dumplings.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶包饺子时系着一条花围裙。
senses.why: The core image is cloth hung in front as a shield; this is the direct, oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是布片挡在身前作屏障；这是该词最直接、最古老的用法。

senses.title: A protective surface or strip resembling an apron
senses.titleCN: 类似围裙的护面或护带
senses.definition: a surface or strip that protects or covers something, shaped like the front protection of an apron
senses.definitionCN: 形似围裙前襟、起保护或覆盖作用的表面或条带
senses.example: The road was rebuilt with a concrete apron at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 道路重修时，入口处铺了混凝土护面。
senses.why: Something spread out in front to protect looks like an apron worn in front of the body.
senses.whyCN: 铺展在前方起保护作用之物，形似穿在身前作保护的围裙。

senses.title: The airport area where aircraft park
senses.definition: the hard-surfaced area of an airport where planes park, load, and are serviced
senses.definitionCN: 机场内飞机停放、装卸与维护的硬化地面区域
senses.example: Ground staff guided the plane to the apron after landing.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机降落后，地勤人员将它引导到停机坪。
senses.why: The paved area spreads out in front of the terminal like a protective apron around the aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 航站楼前的硬化场地铺展延伸，如围裙般环护飞机，故得此名。

senses.title: The front edge of a stage
senses.definition: the part of a stage that extends in front of the curtain toward the audience
senses.definitionCN: 舞台幕布之前、向观众席延伸的部分
senses.example: The actor stepped onto the apron to speak to the audience directly.
senses.exampleCN: 演员走上台口，直接面向观众说话。
senses.why: The stage floor juts forward beyond the main area, apron-like, reaching toward the seats.
senses.whyCN: 台面向主舞台之外前伸，形如围裙的裙摆探向观众席。

intro.en: Apron is a famous case of a word losing an n: it came from napron through misdivision.
intro.cn: apron 是「丢失字母 n」的著名案例：由 napron 经错误切分而来。

items.en: Old French naperon, a diminutive of nape (tablecloth), from Latin mappa (cloth).
items.cn: 古法语 naperon，是 nape（桌布）的小称形式，源自拉丁语 mappa（布）。

items.en: Borrowed into Middle English as napron, meaning a small cloth or protecting cloth.
items.cn: 十四世纪进入中古英语，作 napron，义为小块布或护身之布。

items.en: a napron was misheard and re-cut as an apron, moving the n to the previous word; a napron became an apron.
items.cn: a napron 被误听并重新切分为 an apron，字母 n 移给了前一个冠词，napron 变成了 apron。

items.en: The new form apron established itself in the 1400s and 1500s and became the standard spelling.
items.cn: 新形式 apron 在十五至十六世纪站稳脚跟，成为标准拼写。

items.en: The sense spread from the kitchen garment to protective strips, the airport apron, and the stage apron.
items.cn: 词义从厨房围裙扩展到护面、机场停机坪和舞台台口。

note.en: Watch out for sound-alikes and related protective cloth words.
note.cn: 注意发音相近词及相关防护布类词。

entries.definition: a small cloth for wiping the mouth; shares the French root nape
entries.definitionCN: 餐巾；与 apron 同源于法语 nape（桌布）

entries.definition: table linen, an old word from the same French root
entries.definitionCN: 桌布餐巾类织物；源自同一法语词根的旧词

entries.definition: to try to do something; only the opening letters look similar
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；仅开头拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a loose protective garment, often worn by artists or workers
entries.definitionCN: 罩衫；宽松防护衣，多为画师或工人所穿

entries.definition: protective clothing worn over ordinary clothes, often with sleeves and legs
entries.definitionCN: 工装裤/罩衣；覆盖面比围裙更大的防护服

entries.definition: informal word for the airport parking area, near apron in sense 03
entries.definitionCN: 停机坪（口语说法），与 apron 第 3 义项近义

normalIntro.en: Remember the lost n and the picture of the cloth in front.
normalIntro.cn: 记住那个丢失的 n 和「挡身前的布」的画面。

normal.en: a napron -> an apron: the n jumped from the noun to the article.
normal.cn: a napron → an apron：字母 n 从名词跳到了冠词上。

normal.en: napkin and apron are cousins: both come from nape, the French word for tablecloth.
normal.cn: napkin 与 apron 是亲戚：都来自法语 nape（桌布）。

normal.en: apron strings is a fixed phrase: under one's apron strings means being controlled by someone.
normal.cn: apron strings（围裙带）是固定搭配，under one's apron strings 指「在某人掌控下」。

normal.en: Sound link: 'AY-pron' sounds like 'A-pron' — just the article A plus pron.
normal.cn: 读音联想「诶-普伦」：就像冠词 A 加 pron，好记它的来历。

normal.en: Airport apron: the ground apron-like in front of the terminal where planes park.
normal.cn: 机场停机坪：航站楼前铺展如围裙的地面，飞机停在那里。

abstract.en: Picture a shield made of cloth hanging in front of you.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布做的盾牌挂在身前。

abstract.en: Apron is protection you wear; armor is protection you fight in.
abstract.cn: apron 是穿着的防护，armor 是上阵的铠甲。

abstract.en: One n walked away from napron and never came back.
abstract.cn: 一个字母 n 从 napron 里出走，再也没有回来。

examples.en: She wiped her wet hands on her apron.
examples.cn: 她在围裙上擦了擦湿手。

examples.en: Pilots and ground crews work together on the apron.
examples.cn: 飞行员和地勤人员在停机坪上协同工作。

examples.en: An apron keeps oil stains off your clothes while cooking.
examples.cn: 做饭时围裙能防止油渍弄脏衣服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶铺龙」——诶，围裙一铺开像条小龙挡在身前，油点都溅不到衣服。

root: 源自拉丁语 mappa（布）→ 古法语 nape（桌布）→ naperon（小桌布，护身之布）→ 中古英语 napron → 因误切分 an apron 失去首字母 n。词形演变脉络清晰，misdivision（错误切分）是语言学上著名案例。

sensesIntro.en: From the cloth in front of the body, the word spreads to any apron-like protective area.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「身前的布」出发，词义扩展到一切形似围裙的防护区域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth spread in front as a protective shield
core.cn: 核心意象：铺展在身前、起保护作用的布

branches.en: The kitchen garment that keeps clothes clean.
Any protective surface shaped like a front shield.
The airport ground that spreads before the terminal.
branches.cn: 航站楼前铺展的机场停机坪。

branches.en: The stage floor reaching toward the audience.
branches.cn: 伸向观众席的舞台前缘。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of front protection.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「在前防护」的观念。

intro.en: Apron is a simple noun with few affixes; its story is in sound change, not building blocks.
intro.cn: apron 是个朴素的名词，几乎不用词缀；它的故事在语音演变，而非构词部件。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source mappa also gave the word map.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源 mappa 还派生出 map（地图）一词。

items.example: Mappa is the far source of apron.
items.exampleCN: mappa 是 apron 的远期词源。

items.example: Nape narrowed to mean linen cloth in Old French.
items.exampleCN: nape 在古法语中收窄为餐布之义。

items.example: Napron lost its n through misdivision.
items.exampleCN: napron 因误切分丢掉了首字母 n。

items.example: Napkin keeps the n that apron lost.
items.exampleCN: napkin 保留了 apron 丢失的 n。

items.example: Napery is an old word for household linen.
items.exampleCN: napery 是家用布艺的旧称。

items.example: The aproned cook stirred the soup.
items.exampleCN: 系着围裙的厨师搅动着汤。

latinEntries.example: Mappa mundi once meant a cloth map of the world.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mappa mundi 原指绘在布上的世界地图。

definition_zh: 任意的；随意的；专断的；武断的
definition_en: based on personal choice rather than reason, or using power without limits
core_image: 裁判随手一指，全凭个人喜好
scene: 规则没有写明，全凭他一句话决定。The choice of colour seemed arbitrary rather than planned.
sceneCN: 这里 arbitrary 是「随意的」（第 1 个义项：出于个人选择而非理由）；句意是颜色的选择看上去是随手定的，而非事先规划。

derivatives.zh: 动词：仲裁，同出 arbiter 一词

senses.title: Chosen at random
senses.definition: decided by personal whim rather than by a rule
senses.definitionCN: 凭个人一时喜好决定，而非依据规则
senses.example: The order of the names on the list is arbitrary.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上名字的排序是随意的。
senses.why: Latin arbitrarius described whatever depended on the will of an arbiter, so the word began as 'left to choice'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arbitrarius 指「取决于仲裁者意志的」，所以这个词一开始就是「交由选择决定」的意思。

senses.title: Using power without restraint
senses.definition: acting on will alone, with no check from law or others
senses.definitionCN: 只凭意志行事，不受法律或他人约束
senses.example: The ruler made arbitrary arrests without any charge.
senses.exampleCN: 统治者不做任何指控就随意抓人。
senses.why: When the will belongs to a person with power, 'left to choice' turns into 'answerable to nobody', which is the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 当这种意志属于掌权者时，「交由选择」就变成「不受任何人约束」，这就是政治上的专断义。

intro.en: Arbitrary comes from the Latin word for a judge who decides by his own will.
intro.cn: arbitrary 源自拉丁语中表示「凭自己意志裁决的法官」的词。

items.en: arbiter meant 'judge, witness, one who decides'.
items.cn: arbiter 意为「法官、见证人、裁决者」。

items.en: arbitrium meant 'judgment, will, choice'.
items.cn: arbitrium 意为「判断、意志、选择」。

items.en: arbitrarius meant 'depending on the will'.
items.cn: arbitrarius 意为「取决于意志的」。

items.en: English borrowed it for decisions resting on mere will.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指仅凭意志作出的决定。

items.en: The sense widened from one judge's will to any unchecked power.
items.cn: 词义从一位法官的意志扩展到任何不受制约的权力。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same judge root; the near-meaning group gives other words for will without reason.
note.cn: 形近组同出「裁决者」词根；近义组是其他表示无理性凭意志的词。

normalIntro.en: Arbitrary means the will decides and nothing else does.
normalIntro.cn: arbitrary 意为只由意志决定，别无其他依据。

normal.en: A judge called an arbiter gave the word its root.
normal.cn: 名为 arbiter 的裁决者给了它词根。

normal.en: Arbitrary rules are the opposite of measured ones.
normal.cn: arbitrary 的规定与有依据的规定相反。

normal.en: The adverb is arbitrarily, often used in complaints.
normal.cn: 副词 arbitrarily 常用于抱怨的语境。

normal.en: Arbitration keeps the same root but means fair judging.
normal.cn: arbitration 同根，却表示公平裁断。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-bi-tra-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-bi-tra-ry。

abstract.en: See a finger pointing at one name without reason.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指毫无理由地点中一个名字。

abstract.en: See a ruler's hand signing without reading.
abstract.cn: 想象掌权者不看内容就签字。

abstract.en: See dice thrown to settle a question.
abstract.cn: 想象掷骰子来决定一个问题。

examples.en: The order of the names on the list is arbitrary.
examples.cn: 名单上名字的排序是随意的。

examples.en: The ruler made arbitrary arrests without any charge.
examples.cn: 统治者不做任何指控就随意抓人。

examples.en: Critics called the deadline arbitrary and unfair.
examples.cn: 批评者称这个期限既武断又不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: arbiter（裁决者）加 -ary：裁决者想怎么定就怎么定，于是成了随意的、专断的。

root: 来自拉丁语 arbitrarius「取决于意志的」，源自动词 arbiter「裁决者」与 arbitrium「判断、意志」；由「凭裁决者意志」引申出随意与专断两义。

sensesIntro.en: One root covers both a casual choice and a ruler who answers to no one.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词根既涵盖随手的选择，也涵盖不受约束的掌权者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to point at one option out of many.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在众多选项里随手点向其中一个。

intro.en: A word about will and judgment that split into fairness and its opposite.
intro.cn: 这个词讲的是意志与判断，后来既生出公正，也生出不公。

latinIntro.en: The root arbiter, 'judge', also gives arbitrate and arbitration.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 arbiter「裁决者」也派生出 arbitrate 与 arbitration。

items.meaning: able to be settled by a judge

definition_zh: 拱；拱门；足弓；拱起；首要的（构词前缀义）
definition_en: a curved structure that spans an opening and supports weight above it, or a curved shape resembling this
core_image: 一块块楔形石互相挤压，把上方的重量沿曲线传到两侧墙脚
scene: 石桥下的圆弧把整条桥面托住，石缝里长着细草。The stone arch carries the weight of the wall above it without any wooden beam.
sceneCN: 这里 arch 指「跨越开口并把上方重量分散到两侧的拱形结构」（第 1 个义项：拱）；句意为这道石拱不用木梁就承住了上方的墙。图中可辨识物件：石桥、圆弧、楔形石、墙脚。

pos.zh: 首要的；为首的（多作构词成分）

senses.title: A curved spanning structure
senses.definition: a curved structure that spans an opening and carries weight by compression
senses.definitionCN: 跨越开口、靠受压传递重量的曲线结构
senses.example: The arch turns the downward load into a sideways thrust.
senses.exampleCN: 拱把向下的荷载转为向两侧的推力。
senses.why: the word first named a bow, and a bent bow is exactly the shape that carries weight by compression.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指弓，而弯弓正是靠受压承重的形状。

senses.title: A gateway with a curved top
senses.definition: an opening in a wall topped by a curve, often built as a monument
senses.definitionCN: 墙上的曲线顶开口，常作为纪念性建筑
senses.example: The triumphal arch marks the old entrance to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 那座凯旋门标记着城市的旧入口。
senses.why: when the structure is mostly an opening, the word names the gateway rather than the engineering.
senses.whyCN: 当结构主要是一个开口时，这个词指门本身，而非工程原理。

senses.title: The arch of the foot
senses.definition: the curved instep of the human foot, formed by bones and ligaments
senses.definitionCN: 由骨骼与韧带形成的人脚背曲线
senses.example: The arch of the foot acts as a spring with every step.
senses.exampleCN: 每走一步，足弓都像弹簧一样工作。
senses.why: the body has its own spanning curves, so the architectural word was applied to anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 身体自身就有跨度的曲线，因此建筑词被用到解剖上。

senses.title: The brow's curve
senses.definition: the bony ridge above the eye
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛上方的骨质隆起
senses.example: A heavy arch above the eyes gives the skull a stern look.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛上方厚重的眉弓让头骨显得严厉。
senses.why: any bony curve can be called an arch, and the brow is the most visible one.
senses.whyCN: 任何骨质曲线都可叫 arch，而眉弓是最显眼的一处。

senses.title: Anything shaped like a bow
senses.definition: a curved object or line, such as a rainbow or a row of trees
senses.definitionCN: 弯曲的物体或线条，如彩虹或一排行道树
senses.example: A pale arch of light stood over the valley after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后，一道浅色光弧立在山谷上方。
senses.why: the shape sense is older than the building sense and survives in descriptions of nature.
senses.whyCN: 形状义比建筑义更古老，并在自然描写中留存。

senses.title: To curve upward or over
senses.definition: to bend into a curve, or to span something in a curve
senses.definitionCN: 弯成曲线，或以曲线跨越某物
senses.example: The cat arched its back at the sound of the door.
senses.exampleCN: 听到门响，猫弓起了背。
senses.why: the verb is simply the shape turned into motion, and it applies to bodies, branches and eyebrows.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把形状变成动作，适用于身体、枝条与眉毛。

senses.title: Chief or principal
senses.definition: in compounds, first or foremost, as in arch-enemy or arch-criminal
senses.definitionCN: 在复合词中表示第一位的、为首的，如头号敌人或首恶
senses.example: He became the arch-rival of the reigning champion.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了在位冠军的头号对手。
senses.why: this sense has a different source: a Greek word for leader, not the Latin word for bow.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同：它来自希腊语「首领」，而非拉丁语「弓」。

senses.title: A shoe's arch support
senses.definition: the raised part inside a shoe that supports the instep
senses.definitionCN: 鞋内托住脚背的隆起部分
senses.example: The insole's arch takes the pressure off the heel.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋垫的足弓部分减轻了脚跟压力。
senses.why: shoemaking borrowed the anatomical word for the part of the foot it must hold.
senses.whyCN: 制鞋业借用了这个解剖词，指它必须托住的那部分脚。

intro.en: English arch is two words that look alike: a Latin bow and a Greek leader. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语 arch 是两个形似的词：一个来自拉丁语「弓」，一个来自希腊语「首领」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arcus meant a bow or a curved arc, and it named both the weapon and the shape.
items.cn: arcus 指弓或弧线，既命名武器也命名形状。

items.en: Old French arche carried the architectural sense into English, where it named a curved span.
items.cn: 古法语 arche 把建筑义带入英语，指曲线跨度。

items.en: Separately, Greek arkhos meant leader or chief, and its combining form entered English as a prefix.
items.cn: 另一方面，希腊语 arkhos 意为首领，其组合形式作为前缀进入英语。

items.en: From the twelfth century the pointed and round arch drove Gothic and Romanesque building.
items.cn: 从十二世纪起，尖拱与圆拱推动了哥特式与罗曼式建筑。

items.en: The same shape word was applied to the instep and the brow because both are curved supports.
items.cn: 同一个形状词被用于脚背与眉部，因为两者都是曲线支撑。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of arcus is not established, and the Greek leader word has a separate disputed origin, so the two are not related despite identical spelling.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：arcus 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明，希腊语「首领」词另有争议来源；两者拼写相同但并无亲缘关系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the Latin bow family or easily mistaken for them; group two holds curved structures and shapes.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「弓」一族或容易误认的词；第二组是曲线结构与形状。

entries.definition: A part of a circle, or an electric discharge across a gap; both come from the same Latin bow word.
entries.definitionCN: 圆周的一段，或跨越间隙的放电；两义都来自同一个拉丁「弓」词。

entries.definition: A person who shoots with a bow; it comes from the same Latin source but names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 用弓射箭的人；同出拉丁来源，但指人。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning chief, from Greek; it is unrelated to the Latin bow and must be read separately.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「首领」的前缀，来自希腊语；与拉丁「弓」无关，须分开理解。

entries.definition: A passage under an arch; it is arch plus way, a covered route rather than the structure alone.
entries.definitionCN: 拱下的通道；由 arch 加 way 构成，指有顶路线而非单独结构。

entries.definition: An arched ceiling over a space; an arch spans an opening in a wall, while a vault covers a room.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖空间的拱形顶棚；arch 跨越墙上的开口，vault 覆盖房间。

entries.definition: A curved roof over a round space; it is an arch rotated around a centre.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖圆形空间的曲面屋顶；是绕中心旋转的拱。

entries.definition: A straight structural member carrying load; it works by bending, while an arch works by compression.
entries.definitionCN: 承受荷载的直构件，靠弯曲工作；而拱靠受压工作。

entries.definition: Any line that bends; an arch is one kind of curve with a structural job.
entries.definitionCN: 任何弯曲的线；arch 是带有结构任务的一种曲线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real bow root, the real anatomy words and the separate Greek prefix.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「弓」词根、真实的解剖词与另一个希腊语前缀。

normal.en: The Latin root means bow, so the structure and the weapon share one curved shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为弓，因此结构与武器共有一个弯曲的形状。

normal.en: The family runs arch, arched, archer, archery, archway, archwise.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arch、arched、archer、archery、archway、archwise。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: stone arch, arch bridge, arch of the foot, arch enemy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：石拱、拱桥、足弓、头号敌人。

normal.en: The curve works by squeezing: each stone pushes its neighbour and the load slides down the legs.
normal.cn: 这条曲线靠挤压工作：每块石头推着邻石，荷载沿两侧墙脚滑下。

normal.en: The chief sense is a different word: Greek leader, not Latin bow.
normal.cn: 「首要」义是另一个词：希腊语首领，而非拉丁语弓。

abstract.en: Picture a row of stones learning to lean on each other so none falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一排石头学会彼此倚靠，于是一块也不落。

abstract.en: Picture a rainbow that has been asked to hold up a bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一道彩虹被请求去托住一座桥。

abstract.en: Picture an eyebrow as a small bridge over an eye.
abstract.cn: 想象眉毛是一只眼睛上方的小桥。

examples.en: The bridge's arch has stood for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座桥的拱已立了六百年。

examples.en: High arches support the soles of runners.
examples.cn: 高足弓支撑着跑者的脚底。

examples.en: The two companies are arch rivals in the same market.
examples.cn: 这两家公司在同一市场是头号对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: arcus（弓）→ 弯成弓形的承重结构 → 拱；同形前缀又表示「首领」

root: 名词 arch 来自拉丁 arcus「弓、弧」，经古法语 arche 入英语；表示「首领」的 arch- 另有希腊语 arkhos 来源，二者拼写相同但无亲缘。英语 arch。arcus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one curve: a bow becomes a span, then a gateway, then the body's own arches, then any curved shape, a verb, a separate 'chief' prefix and finally a shoe part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条曲线展开：弓成为跨度，再成为门、身体自身的弓、任何弯曲形状、动词，另有一条「首领」前缀义，最后落到鞋内支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wedge-shaped stones leaning on one another so the load travels down both legs.
core.cn: 核心意象：楔形石块彼此倚靠，使荷载沿两侧墙脚传下。

branches.en: THE CURVE: a structural span and a rainbow are the same bowed line with and without a job.
branches.cn: 曲线：承重跨度与彩虹，是同一条弓形线，一条有任务，一条没有。

branches.en: THE GATEWAY: when the opening matters more than the engineering, the arch becomes a door.
branches.cn: 门：当开口比工程更重要时，拱就成了门。

branches.en: THE BODY: the foot, the brow and the shoe all repeat the same small bridge.
branches.cn: 身体：脚、眉与鞋都重复着同一座小桥。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the shape becomes a verb when a back or a branch bends.
branches.cn: 动作：当背或枝条弯曲时，形状变成动词。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: the 'chief' sense is a Greek leader, not a Latin bow.
branches.cn: 另一个词：「首要」义是希腊语首领，而非拉丁语弓。

intro.en: Arch is a Latin bow noun plus a separate Greek leader prefix, so the affix list must keep the two lines apart.
intro.cn: arch 是一个拉丁语「弓」名词加上一个独立的希腊语「首领」前缀，因此词缀清单必须把两条线分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin arcus gives arc, arch, archer and archery; the prefix arch- comes from Greek arkhos and is not a relative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 给出 arc、arch、archer 与 archery；表示「首领」的前缀来自希腊语 arkhos，并非同族。

items.example: Arcus named the weapon and the curve.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既指武器也指曲线。

items.example: The arc of the bridge is shallow.
An arched window lights the stair.

items.meaning: the sport of shooting with a bow

items.example: The archway leads to the courtyard.
An arch-rival is the chief rival.
items.exampleCN: 头号对手就是最主要的对手。

definition_zh: 建筑师；设计师；缔造者
definition_en: a person who designs buildings, or someone who creates a plan for something larger
core_image: 伏在图纸上勾出房屋轮廓的人
scene: 工地边站着一个人，手里卷着图纸。The architect walked through the half-built house.
sceneCN: 这里 architect 是「建筑师」（第 1 个义项：设计建筑的人）；句意是建筑师走过那栋建了一半的房子。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：建筑的；建筑学的

senses.title: A designer of buildings
senses.definition: someone whose job is to plan how a building will be made
senses.definitionCN: 以规划建筑物如何建造为职业的人
senses.example: The architect walked through the half-built house.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师走过那栋建了一半的房子。
senses.why: Greek tekton meant 'builder' and arkhi- meant 'chief', so an architect was the chief builder who set the plan.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 tekton 意为「建造者」，arkhi- 意为「首要的」，所以 architect 原本是定下方案的营造主事者。

senses.title: A creator of a larger plan
senses.definition: a person who shapes an idea, system, or event
senses.definitionCN: 塑造某个理念、制度或事件的人
senses.example: She was the architect of the peace agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这份和平协议的缔造者。
senses.why: The building metaphor moves easily to any structure: whoever draws the plan of a system is its architect.
senses.whyCN: 建筑的比喻很容易移用到任何结构上：谁画出某个体系的蓝图，谁就是它的缔造者。

intro.en: Architect is a Greek compound meaning 'chief builder'.
intro.cn: architect 是一个希腊语复合词，意为「首要的建造者」。

items.en: arkhi- meant 'chief, leading'.
items.cn: arkhi- 意为「首要的、领头的」。

items.en: tekton meant 'builder, carpenter'.
items.cn: tekton 意为「建造者、木匠」。

items.en: arkhitekton was the master builder who set the design.
items.cn: arkhitekton 指定下设计的营造主事者。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as architectus.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 architectus。

items.en: English architect kept the sense of the one who plans before others build.
items.cn: 英语 architect 保留了「在他人动工之前先做规划者」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same word family; the near-meaning group gives other planners.
note.cn: 形近组是同一词族；近义组是其他做规划的人。

entries.definition: one who plans how a thing looks

normalIntro.en: An architect is the chief of the builders.
normalIntro.cn: architect 就是建造者中的主事者。

normal.en: The first part arch- appears in archbishop and arch-enemy.
normal.cn: 前半 arch- 也出现在 archbishop 与 arch-enemy 中。

normal.en: The ending -tect means builder, as in tectonic.
normal.cn: 结尾 -tect 意为建造者，tectonic 亦同源。

normal.en: The plural simply adds -s.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 -s。

normal.en: Used of people, it means the one who shaped a plan.
normal.cn: 用于人时，指塑造出方案的那一位。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-chi-tect.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-chi-tect。

abstract.en: See a rolled drawing under one arm.
abstract.cn: 想象腋下夹着一卷图纸。

abstract.en: See a pencil tracing a roof line.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔勾出屋顶的线。

abstract.en: See a figure standing where a wall will rise.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在将要砌墙的位置。

examples.en: The architect walked through the half-built house.
examples.cn: 建筑师走过那栋建了一半的房子。

examples.en: She was the architect of the peace agreement.
examples.cn: 她是这份和平协议的缔造者。

examples.en: The architects submitted three designs for the library.
examples.cn: 建筑师们为图书馆提交了三份设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: arch-（首要）加 tect（建造）：领头的建造者，就是建筑师。

root: 源自希腊语 arkhitekton，由 arkhi-「首要」与 tekton「建造者」构成，经拉丁语 architectus 进入英语；由「营造主事者」引申为任何体系的缔造者。

sensesIntro.en: The chief builder of walls became the planner of anything with a structure.
sensesIntro.cn: 砌墙的主事者，后来成了任何有结构之物的规划者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand drawing a line that will become a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手画下的线，将来会变成一堵墙。

branches.en: the chief architect of the plan

intro.en: A Greek compound that English borrowed whole.
intro.cn: 这是一个被英语整体借入的希腊语复合词。

latinIntro.en: The same tekton, 'builder', underlies tectonic and technology.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个 tekton「建造者」也是 tectonic 与 technology 的来源。

definition_zh: 建筑学；建筑风格；体系架构
definition_en: the art and study of designing buildings, the style of a building, or the structure of a system
core_image: 石柱与钢梁搭出的整体秩序
scene: 那条街两旁的房子年代相差很远。The architecture of the old town draws many visitors.
sceneCN: 这里 architecture 是「建筑风格」（第 2 个义项：建筑呈现出的样式）；句意是老城的建筑吸引了许多游客。

pos.zh: 名词：建筑学；建筑风格；架构

senses.title: The study of building design
senses.definition: the subject and profession of planning buildings
senses.definitionCN: 规划建筑物的学科与职业
senses.example: He studied architecture in Rome for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在罗马学了五年建筑学。
senses.why: The suffix -ure turns the person architect into the field itself, the whole body of knowledge about planning buildings.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ure 把「人」变成「领域」，指关于建筑规划的一整套知识。

senses.title: The style of buildings
senses.definition: the characteristic form of buildings from a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某时期建筑呈现的典型样式
senses.example: The architecture of the old town draws many visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 老城的建筑吸引了许多游客。
senses.why: Since a style is the visible result of design, the name of the craft came to label what the craft produces.
senses.whyCN: 既然风格是设计的可见成果，这门手艺的名称也就用来指它造出来的样子。

senses.title: The structure of a system
senses.definition: the way the parts of a computer or organization are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或组织中各部分被安排的方式
senses.example: The team redesigned the software architecture last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队去年重新设计了软件架构。
senses.why: Buildings are the model for any ordered whole, so architects' word serves for the frame of software and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是任何有序整体的模型，于是建筑业的词被用来指软件与制度的骨架。

intro.en: Architecture is the noun of office built on the Greek word for a master builder.
intro.cn: architecture 是在希腊语「营造主事者」基础上构成的表示职业的名词。

items.en: The master builder was called arkhitekton.
items.cn: 营造主事者称为 arkhitekton。

items.en: Latin formed architectura for the art itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语造出 architectura 指这门技艺。

items.en: French passed the word on in its modern shape.
items.cn: 法语以现代形态把这个词传下去。

items.en: English used it for both the craft and its style.
items.cn: 英语用它兼指这门技艺与它呈现的风格。

items.en: Computing extended it to the layout of systems.
items.cn: 计算机领域又把它扩展到系统的布局。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the architect stem; the near-meaning group names other ordered wholes.
note.cn: 形近组保留 architect 词干；近义组是其他表示有序整体的词。

entries.definition: a plan for how a thing is made

normalIntro.en: Architecture is what an architect knows and makes.
normalIntro.cn: architecture 就是建筑师所懂与所造的东西。

normal.en: It names a subject as well as a style.
normal.cn: 它既指学科，也指风格。

normal.en: In computing it means the frame of a system.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域指系统的框架。

normal.en: The adjective is architectural.
normal.cn: 形容词是 architectural。

normal.en: It has no plural in ordinary use.
normal.cn: 日常使用中没有复数。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-chi-tec-ture.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-chi-tec-ture。

abstract.en: See columns holding up a wide roof.
abstract.cn: 想象石柱撑起宽阔的屋顶。

abstract.en: See a floor plan laid over a real room.
abstract.cn: 想象平面图叠在真实房间上。

abstract.en: See boxes and arrows forming a system.
abstract.cn: 想象方框与箭头组成一个系统。

examples.en: He studied architecture in Rome for five years.
examples.cn: 他在罗马学了五年建筑学。

examples.en: The architecture of the old town draws many visitors.
examples.cn: 老城的建筑吸引了许多游客。

examples.en: The team redesigned the software architecture last year.
examples.cn: 这个团队去年重新设计了软件架构。

dict_mnemonic.text: architect（建筑师）加 -ure：建筑师所从事的学问，就是建筑学。

root: 源自拉丁语 architectura，来自希腊语 arkhitekton「营造主事者」；由「建造的技艺」发展出学科、风格与架构三义。

sensesIntro.en: One noun covers the craft, the look it produces, and any well-built frame.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词涵盖这门技艺、它造就的外观，以及任何搭建良好的骨架。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone and steel arranged into a standing order.
core.cn: 核心意象：石与钢被安排成站得住的秩序。

intro.en: A Latin noun of craft built on a Greek compound.
intro.cn: 这是一个在希腊语复合词基础上构成的拉丁语技艺名词。

latinIntro.en: The builder root tekton also appears in tectonic and technology.
latinIntro.cn: 建造者词根 tekton 也出现在 tectonic 与 technology 中。

definition_zh: 区域；地区；面积；领域
definition_en: a part of a place, the measure of a surface, or a field of activity
core_image: 在地上画出的一个圈，圈内算一处
scene: 到处的屋顶都压得很低。The area around the station is full of small shops.
sceneCN: 这里 area 是「区域」（第 1 个义项：某一片地方）；句意是车站周围一带全是小店。

senses.title: A part of a place
senses.definition: a particular part of a town, country, or surface
senses.definitionCN: 城镇、国家或地面上某个特定部分
senses.example: The area around the station is full of small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 车站周围一带全是小店。
senses.why: Latin area first meant a flat open space, so any bounded patch of ground took the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 area 原指一块平坦的空地，因此任何划出边界的土地都用这个词。

senses.title: The size of a surface
senses.definition: the amount of flat space that something covers
senses.definitionCN: 某物覆盖的平面空间有多大
senses.example: The kitchen has an area of twelve square metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这间厨房的面积是十二平方米。
senses.why: Since area named the flat patch itself, measuring that patch produced the sense of surface size.
senses.whyCN: 既然 area 本指那块平面，度量这块平面就产生了「面积」义。

senses.title: A field of activity
senses.definition: a subject or type of work with its own boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 有自身边界的学科或工作范围
senses.example: She works in the area of child health.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事儿童健康领域的工作。
senses.why: The image of a marked-out patch transfers to knowledge: a field is a bounded space of study.
senses.whyCN: 「划出的一块地」这一形象被移用到知识上：领域就是有边界的研究空间。

intro.en: Area is a Latin word for an open piece of level ground.
intro.cn: area 是拉丁语词，指一块平坦开阔的地面。

items.en: area meant 'open space, threshing floor'.
items.cn: area 意为「空地、打谷场」。

items.en: Roman writers used it for the extent of a surface.
items.cn: 罗马作家用它指平面的范围。

items.en: English took it for a cleared or bounded space.
items.cn: 英语借入，指清出或划出边界的空间。

items.en: The mathematical sense of surface measure became regular.
items.cn: 数学上「表面积」的用法固定下来。

items.en: The word spread to any field of study or activity.
items.cn: 这个词又扩展到任何学科或活动范围。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the same short stem; the near-meaning group gives other words for parts of space.
note.cn: 形近组共享同一词干；近义组是其他表示空间部分的词。

entries.definition: a large part of a country
an area with a special use

normalIntro.en: An area is a piece of ground with a line around it.
normalIntro.cn: area 就是被一条线圈起来的一块地。

normal.en: It covers both a place and its measured size.
normal.cn: 它既指地点，也指量出的大小。

normal.en: In the area of introduces a field of work.
normal.cn: in the area of 引出某个工作领域。

normal.en: The plural is simply areas.
normal.cn: 复数直接写 areas。

normal.en: It is common in place names such as the London area.
normal.cn: 它常用于地名，如伦敦一带。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AIR-i-a.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AIR-i-a。

abstract.en: See a chalk circle drawn on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象地板上用粉笔画出的圈。

abstract.en: See a tape measure run across a room.
abstract.cn: 想象卷尺横过一间屋子。

abstract.en: See a map divided into shaded patches.
abstract.cn: 想象地图被分成一块块阴影。

examples.en: The area around the station is full of small shops.
examples.cn: 车站周围一带全是小店。

examples.en: The kitchen has an area of twelve square metres.
examples.cn: 这间厨房的面积是十二平方米。

examples.en: She works in the area of child health.
examples.cn: 她从事儿童健康领域的工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 area 想成地上画出的一块空地：既是地点，也是这块地的面积。

root: 直接借自拉丁语 area「空地、打谷场」，由「划出边界的平面」发展出地区、面积与领域三义。

sensesIntro.en: A piece of flat ground gives a place, a measurement, and then a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 一块平地先给出地点，再给出度量，最后给出研究领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chalk circle closing off a patch of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：粉笔圈出的一小块地面。

intro.en: A short Latin noun that English took without change.
intro.cn: 这是一个英语原样借入的简短拉丁名词。

latinIntro.en: The adjective areal is the main English formation from it.
latinIntro.cn: 由它构成的主要英语派生词是形容词 areal。

items.meaning: a smaller part of an area

definition_zh: 争论；争辩；论证；主张
definition_en: to disagree in words, to give reasons for an opinion, or to persuade someone by reasoning
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子各说各的理由
scene: 饭桌上两个人声音越来越高。They argued about who should pay the bill.
sceneCN: 这里 argue 是「争论」（第 1 个义项：因意见不合而口头冲突）；句意是他们为谁该付账争了起来。

senses.title: To disagree in words
senses.definition: to speak angrily with someone who disagrees
senses.definitionCN: 与意见不同的人激烈地说话
senses.example: They argued about who should pay the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为谁该付账争了起来。
senses.why: Latin arguere meant 'to make clear by reasoning'; when two people each press their case, clarity turns into conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arguere 意为「通过论证说清楚」；当双方各自坚持说法时，说清就变成了冲突。

senses.title: To give reasons for a view
senses.definition: to present evidence and reasoning in support of an opinion
senses.definitionCN: 提出证据与推理来支持某个观点
senses.example: The report argues that the plan will save money.
senses.exampleCN: 报告论证说这项计划能省钱。
senses.why: This keeps the original Latin sense: to argue is to lay out proofs so that a conclusion becomes clear.
senses.whyCN: 这一义保留了拉丁语原义：argue 就是摆出证据，使结论变得清楚。

senses.title: To persuade by reasoning
senses.definition: to bring someone to a decision through argument
senses.definitionCN: 通过论理使人作出某个决定
senses.example: She argued him into taking the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服他接受了这份工作。
senses.why: If reasons can make a point clear, they can also move a listener to act, which gives the persuasive sense.
senses.whyCN: 既然理由能让观点变清楚，也就能推动听者行动，于是产生「说服」义。

intro.en: Argue comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to make clear'.
intro.cn: argue 源自一个意为「使清楚」的拉丁动词。

items.en: arguere meant 'to make clear, to prove'.
items.cn: arguere 意为「使清楚、证明」。

items.en: argumentum was a proof or a statement that clarifies.
items.cn: argumentum 指证明或使事情清楚的说法。

items.en: French arguer meant 'to reason, to dispute'.
items.cn: 法语 arguer 意为「推理、争辩」。

items.en: English argue covered both proving and quarrelling.
items.cn: 英语 argue 兼指论证与争吵。

items.en: The quarrel sense grew commonest in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，争吵义变得最常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the argument stem; the near-meaning group gives other words of dispute and proof.
note.cn: 形近组共享 argument 词干；近义组是其他表示争执与论证的词。

entries.definition: a dispute or a set of reasons

normalIntro.en: To argue is to press a case until it is clear.
normalIntro.cn: argue 就是把一个说法推到清楚为止。

normal.en: Argue that introduces the claim being defended.
normal.cn: argue that 引出所要辩护的主张。

normal.en: Argue with a person, argue about a thing.
normal.cn: 对人用 with，对事用 about。

normal.en: The noun argument drops the final e.
normal.cn: 名词 argument 去掉了词尾的 e。

normal.en: Arguably means it can be reasonably claimed.
normal.cn: arguably 意为「有理由这样说」。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-gue.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-gue。

abstract.en: See two hands gesturing across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手隔着桌子比划。

abstract.en: See a page of numbered reasons.
abstract.cn: 想象一页列着编号理由的纸。

abstract.en: See one figure leaning in to persuade another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人凑近去说服另一个。

examples.en: They argued about who should pay the bill.
examples.cn: 他们为谁该付账争了起来。

examples.en: The report argues that the plan will save money.
examples.cn: 报告论证说这项计划能省钱。

examples.en: She argued him into taking the job.
examples.cn: 她说服他接受了这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: argue 与 argument 同族：把理由摆到台面上讲清楚，讲不拢就成了争吵。

root: 来自拉丁语 arguere「使清楚、证明」，名词 argumentum 指证明；由「说清道理」分化出论证、主张、争吵与说服诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Making a matter clear can end in proof, in persuasion, or in a quarrel.
sensesIntro.cn: 把事情说清楚，结局可能是论证成立，也可能是说服，还可能是吵起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people leaning across a table, each holding a point.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔着桌子前倾，各执一说。

intro.en: A Latin verb of proof that now mostly means to quarrel.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示证明的拉丁动词，如今多半指争吵。

latinIntro.en: The noun argumentum gave English argument.
latinIntro.cn: 名词 argumentum 给出了英语的 argument。
